correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the null problem to a uniform fixed-composition binary word, derives the Cramér–von Mises bridge-energy representation exactly, computes the unconditional bridge second moments hypergeometrically, and conditions a distinguished edge to be a change. Summing the resulting conditional second moments gives the mixed covariance. The small totals are checked separately, and an exact-rational program corroborates the formulas over 8,166 words and 777 conditional aggregate cases.

value.rationale: The claim links two canonical and complementary two-sample diagnostics: local alternation of pooled labels and global quadratic empirical separation. The exact finite-sample sign is uniform over all nontrivial sample-size configurations and the proportional-sample covariance has a simple nonzero limit. This is a structural dependence law, not a routine recomputation of either marginal distribution.
